description: Grounded knowledge corpus for RAGAS evaluation of the RAG_Pipeline. Each passage is a self-contained factual statement. The evaluation questions in ragas_eval.jsonl are answerable strictly from this corpus, so retrieval quality and answer faithfulness can be measured against a known ground truth.

passages.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that combines a retrieval system with a generative language model. Before generating an answer, the system retrieves relevant documents from an external knowledge source and conditions the model's output on that retrieved evidence.

RAG reduces hallucination by grounding generation in retrieved evidence. Because the model answers from supplied context rather than only its parametric memory, its responses are more traceable and less likely to invent unsupported facts.

An embedding model converts text into a fixed-length numerical vector. Texts with similar meaning map to vectors that are close together in the embedding space, which enables semantic similarity search.

A vector store indexes embedding vectors so that, given a query vector, it can quickly return the most similar stored vectors. FAISS is a widely used library for efficient similarity search over dense vectors.

Chunking splits long documents into smaller passages before embedding. Token-aware chunking keeps each chunk within a target token budget and often adds overlap between adjacent chunks so that context spanning a boundary is not lost.

Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and is a common scoring function for semantic retrieval. A higher cosine similarity indicates that a stored chunk is more semantically related to the query.
The top_k parameter controls how many of the most similar chunks the retriever returns for a query. A larger top_k increases recall but can introduce less relevant context.

Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) re-ranks retrieved results to balance relevance to the query against diversity among the selected chunks. The lambda parameter trades off relevance versus diversity; a higher lambda favors relevance.
A similarity threshold filters out retrieved chunks whose similarity score falls below a minimum value. This prevents weakly related context from being passed to the generator.
The guardrail stage inspects retrieved chunks before generation and removes context that is irrelevant or unsafe. It acts as a quality gate between retrieval and generation.
The generator stage takes the user question and the filtered context chunks and prompts the language model to produce a grounded answer that cites the supplied evidence.

The evaluator stage checks the generated answer against the retrieved context and assigns a consistency score. A low consistency score indicates that the answer may contain claims not supported by the context.
Faithfulness in RAGAS measures whether the claims in the generated answer can be inferred from the retrieved context. A faithful answer makes no claims that the context does not support.
Answer relevancy in RAGAS measures how well the generated answer addresses the original question. Answers that are incomplete or contain redundant information receive a lower relevancy score.
Context precision in RAGAS measures whether the relevant chunks are ranked highly among the retrieved context. High precision means useful chunks appear near the top of the retrieved set.
Context recall in RAGAS measures whether the retrieved context contains all the information needed to produce the ground-truth answer. Low recall means the retriever missed necessary evidence.
A correlation ID is an identifier attached to logs and traces so that all records produced while handling a single request can be linked together across components.

OpenTelemetry is an open standard for collecting traces, metrics, and logs from applications. The RAG pipeline emits spans for retrieval, generation, and evaluation so latency can be attributed to each stage.
The pipeline exposes a FastAPI service that accepts a question over HTTP and returns a grounded answer. It supports synchronous responses and health checks for container orchestration.
Offline evaluation runs a fixed dataset of questions through the pipeline in continuous integration so that quality regressions can be detected before changes are merged.
